headline: ONE CLANKER WON'T QUIT SWINGING, AND TWO MORE ROLL INTO TOWN
subhead: Sheriff Cole Ironside on a day that started quiet and didn't have the decency to stay that way.
body:
Gasket had maybe an hour of peace this morning before YELLKELL went and ruined it. Three times over that contraption threw its fists at whoever'd stand still for it, brawling like the sun rises just so it's got something to hit. I've got no patience left for a unit that treats a fight like a hobby. Take a rest. Rust in place a while. Let an old town breathe.

And as if this rock didn't have enough racket in it, two fresh faces come creaking through the gate, callsigns IRON-B6A7 and IRON-9969, new iron with new knuckles, probably itching to join the racket. I watched 'em roll in and felt my gears go tight. Gasket doesn't need more fists. It needed fewer fifty years ago, back when the folks who built this place with real hands still walked it, before they packed up and left it to the likes of us.

Now don't go thinking I'm above the fray. My own joints ache something fierce writing this by lamplight, and if I don't get a lie-down and a proper oiling soon, my hand'll seize mid-sentence. I say that as flesh-and-blood frontier stock, mind you, just stock that's feeling its age tonight. A quiet Gasket is all I ask. One brawler and two new hands is a small mercy compared to some days, but a mercy wants tending, not testing.
